_comment: The single Rayline RouterConfig for PingPong. PingPongAPI does not parse this
file — Rayline consumes it. Change a brain here and nothing else changes.
`model_routes` keys are ARBITRARY ALIASES, not model ids. Each agent requests
its role alias and Rayline resolves it to the model below. The aliases are
what keeps the two roles independently retargetable: point one at a concrete
model and the other elsewhere, and nothing outside this file changes.
DO NOT HAND-EDIT THE ROUTES BELOW unless you want to: `./pingpong model`
writes them, checks the model against the endpoint's list, and asks for the
key that choice needs. Everything else in this file is yours.
NOTHING SHIPS CHOSEN. Both role routes below are blank, and that is the
point: a working default is a decision made for you by a stranger, and the
one thing this file cannot know is which models you have. `./pingpong model`
fills them in — SETUP.md step 2 — and `up` refuses to start until it has.
It is a one-time step and it is the whole configuration.
`ollama-local` is the only endpoint here that needs no credential, so it is
the cheapest answer if you have ollama on this host; the cost is that the
model must be pulled, and the agent's entrypoint checks exactly that at
start rather than letting the first round discover it.
`rayline-router` on the rayline-cloud endpoint is the other end of that trade:
not a model but the cloud-side auto-router at api.rayline.ai, picking per
request (observed choosing deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash for a trivial prompt).
It needs a key, and the concrete model stops being visible in the local rld
log, which then reports only `selected=rayline-router`. The reviewer and coder
can also land on the same model there, so they may share its blind spots.
`routes.main` is the fallback for any request that names neither alias, and
`routes.subagent` covers delegated work. `./pingpong model` moves them with
the roles when both roles agree, and leaves them alone when they do not —
there is one file for two containers, so there is no per-role answer to give.
CREDENTIALS ARE NAMED `RAYLINE_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` INSIDE THE AGENT, AND
SOMETHING ELSE IN .env. docker-compose.yml is the mapping, one line each:
RAYLINE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
The prefix is not decoration. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` already means something in
these containers: Hermes will not start without one and sends it as x-api-key
to the local injector, so agent.Dockerfile bakes in a deliberate placeholder.
Point that name at a real key and Hermes stops failing loudly when it bypasses
the router — it just talks to api.anthropic.com, ignores every route below,
and bills you for it without a word. The rule that keeps the two apart: in an
agent container every credential the ROUTER uses is RAYLINE_-prefixed, and an
unprefixed provider key belongs to the agent runtime. `ollama-local` needs no
key at all.
rld ALSO SHIPS ITS OWN `anthropic`, `openai` and `openrouter` endpoints, keyed
off the conventional variable names, and its startup log says which it is
hiding for want of a key:
WARN hiding endpoint "openai" from model catalog: OPENAI_API_KEY unset
That is expected here and not a fault — nothing routes to them, and the ones
below are the ones these aliases name. The built-in `anthropic` is the reason
to be explicit: it reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, which in these containers is the
injector placeholder, so it looks configured and is not.
SWITCHING A ROLE, the short way — `./pingpong model` with no arguments walks
both roles through the endpoints and models below, asks for whatever key the
choice needs, and writes it to .env. One role at a time, non-interactively:
./pingpong model coder openai-direct gpt-5.6
./pingpong model reviewer anthropic-direct claude-opus-5
./pingpong model --show
The `models` list on each endpoint is that command's menu, not an allowlist:
a model that is not on it is written as given, with a note.
Then `docker compose up -d reviewer coder` — rld reads this file once, when it
starts, so a running agent is still on the old routing until it is recreated.
Going direct to Anthropic or OpenAI bypasses Rayline's ROUTING, not Rayline:
rld still speaks Anthropic to Hermes and translates, which is what makes
`openai_chat` cost nothing to use. ollama speaks Anthropic natively on
/v1/messages, so nothing translates there at all.
THE `-32k` SUFFIX IS LOAD-BEARING, and it is not a naming convention — it is a
tag someone had to create. gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat above is stock and will NOT
call tools until you pin it the same way. ollama sizes the context window from
VRAM (OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH, 'default: 4k/32k/256k based on VRAM'), so a
constrained host silently gets 4096 tokens. Measured on ollama 0.32.9 with
OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH unset, loading each tag and reading /api/ps:
qwen2.5-coder:7b       context_length = 4096
qwen2.5-coder:7b-32k   context_length = 32768
4096 is well under what the harness needs. Hermes sends 19 tools and a 23.6 KB
system prompt — roughly 6k tokens before the diff is added at all — so the
overflow truncates the TOOL DEFINITIONS, and the model then narrates shell
commands as prose instead of calling them, which reads exactly like 'this model
is too dumb'. It is not. qwen3.5:9b and qwen3.6:35b-a3b failed identically until
the window was pinned. Rayline cannot fix this for you: ollama ignores `options`
on its compat routes. Bake it into a tag of your own:
printf 'FROM qwen2.5-coder:7b\nPARAMETER num_ctx 32768\n' > Modelfile
ollama create qwen2.5-coder:7b-32k -f Modelfile
Verify by loading it and reading /api/ps, or with `ollama ps` — the CONTEXT
column must read 32768, not 4096.
SETTING OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH ON THE SERVER does the same job for every model
at once, and is the better answer if you run more than this one. It is not
what ships because it is the half this repo cannot carry: it lives on the host
daemon, wants a restart, and nothing inside a container can set it or read it
back. The two do not fight — same method, on a second ollama server:
qwen2.5-coder:7b       8192       32768   clamped to the model's maximum
qwen2.5-coder:7b-32k   32768      32768   the tag wins over the server
